questions.text: A facade has an oversized recessed portal visible from the street, but the actual door inside the portal is sized for a person. Which distinction is being tested?

options.text: The portal works at visual scale, while the inner door restores human scale.
Both elements prove the building lacks scale because they differ in size.
The portal is only decorative and has no effect on scale perception.
The inner door is a proportioning system rather than a human-scale cue.

rationale.takeaway: Scale questions usually ask what the comparison is: context, normal size, or the body.
rationale.b: Different sizes can clarify, not erase, scale.
rationale.c: A portal can strongly affect scale perception.
rationale.d: A door can signal human scale without being a full proportioning system.

questions.text: A review panel asks why a lobby with the same floor area feels more monumental after its ceiling height is increased. What is the strongest source-backed explanation?

options.text: Floor area alone controls human scale.
Room height has a strong effect on perceived human scale.
Only wall color can make the space feel monumental.

rationale.c: Color may affect perception but is not the only factor.
rationale.d: Scale remains a comparative perception, not a fixed building-type label.
